title: Capital Punishment
rootClaim: The death penalty should be abolished globally as an intolerable violation of human rights and a flawed instrument of state justice.

branches.text: The risk of executing innocent human beings is inevitable due to human error, false testimony, and systemic judicial flaws.

children.text: DNA exonerations demonstrate that numerous individuals have been wrongfully convicted and sentenced to death.
Stringent appellate review procedures and modern forensic standards minimize the error rate down to near-zero in capital cases.
Irreversibility Dilemma: Unlike incarceration, an execution cannot be remedied when post-conviction evidence subsequently emerges.
Epistemic Threshold Argument: Capital punishment could be restricted exclusively to cases with absolute proof (e.g., unambiguous high-definition video or DNA matches).
Socioeconomic and Racial Disparities: Capital sentencing disproportionately targets underprivileged defendants and racial minorities due to implicit jury bias and inadequate legal representation.

branches.text: Retributive Justice: Capital punishment is morally required to inflict proportional punishment for atrocious crimes (lex talionis).

children.text: Just deserts framework dictates that an offender who intentionally deprives an innocent person of life forfeits their own right to life.
Kantian Inviolability of Dignity: Human dignity is inherent and inalienable; state execution degrades society by reducing human life to an instrument of retributive vengeance.
Immanuel Kant explicitly argued that executing a murderer respects their moral agency by treating them as a rational actor accountable for their deeds.
General Deterrence Hypothesis: The threat of execution deters prospective offenders from committing capital offenses far more effectively than prison sentences.
Empirical criminology consistently shows no statistically significant deterrence differential between capital punishment and life without parole.
Most capital murders are committed during severe emotional distress or psychosis, where rational cost-benefit deterrent calculations are absent.

branches.text: Financial Cost: Maintaining capital appeal litigation and specialized death rows costs state treasuries vastly more than housing inmates for life without parole.

children.text: Streamlining capital trial procedures and limiting repetitive appeals would drastically cut administrative expenditure.
Truncating appeal safeguards directly escalates the probability of executing wrongfully convicted innocent defendants.

definitions.description: The principle of retributive justice where punishment corresponds in degree and kind to the offense ('an eye for an eye').
A theory of justice holding that proportional punishment is a morally acceptable response to crime, regardless of outcome utility.
A prison sentence requiring an offender to remain incarcerated for the remainder of their natural life without possibility of release.
Fundamental human rights that cannot be surrendered, transferred, or revoked by state authority.
The required standard or degree of evidential certainty necessary to justify a moral or legal decision.
